chapter: Chicago clubs, entertainers and tent shows
title: Why male blues singers were neglected in the Black press
summary: Cheatham recalls no popular male blues singers on stage, only guitar-playing singers in the South.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: I noticed in going through the black papers of the time, like the Chicago Defender, whenever they talked about blues, this is in the '20's, in their reviews or articles, they're always talking about the women.
They never talk about th e men and if it weren't for the ads, for the records, you wouldn't know that male blues singers existed.
Why do you supposed that was?
Because the males -- I don't think there were any male blues singers. I don't remember any.
Now that may have been, but I don't remember any of them. I remember -- I have heard a lot of male blues singers in the South.
Most of them were guitar players,
also, they played guitar and sang the blues. But I don't remember any real popular blues singer, a male blues singer during that time. I don't.
No, they were sort of neglected.
Neglected, yes. Cause blues singers, you know, they were Mame Mammie Smith and all the rest of them.
They didn't appear. The male blues singers, apparently did not appear on stage.
They didn't I don't remember any of them. Any of them. They were in the background.
